Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 6 NATIONAL AFFAIRS CABINET APPROVALS Cabinet Approves Extension of Jal Jeevan Mission Till 2028 with Enhanced Outlay of Rs 8.69 Lakh Crore In March 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) until 2028 with an enhanced total outlay of Rs 8.69 lakh crore. • The Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS) will also restructure the JJM to shift its focus from infrastructure creation to sustainable service delivery and drinking water governance. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Cabinet approval for extension of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) till December 2028. ✓ Objective: Provide Tap water supply to all rural households ✓ Nodal Ministry: MoJS ✓ New Outlay: Rs 8.69 lakh crore (total); Central assistance – Rs 3.59 lakh crore ✓ New Digital Framework: ‘Sujalam Bharat’ with unique Sujal Gaon/Service Area ID for villages ✓ Community Initiatives: ‘Jal Arpan’ (handover of schemes), ‘Jal Utsav’ (annual maintenance event). ✓ Target: Universal coverage of 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028 ✓ Vision: Viksit Bharat @2047 with 24×7 piped drinking water supply in rural areas Key Features of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (JJM 2.0): Financial Outlay: The Cabinet enhanced the JJM outlay to Rs. 8.69 lakh crore, increasing central assistance to Rs. 3.59 lakh crore, including an additional allocation of Rs. 1.51 lakh crore over the Rs. 2.08 lakh crore approved in 2019–20. Approach: The JJM 2.0 shifts from an infrastructure-centric model to a citizen-centric utility service approach to ensure 24×7 rural drinking water supply aligned with the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. Sujalam: A national digital framework ‘Sujalam Bharat’ will map the entire drinking water system from source to tap, assigning each village a Sujal Gaon / Service Area Identification (ID) for monitoring and transparency. Governance: The Jal Arpan mechanism will ensure transparent handover of water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats (GPs) and Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), while Jal Utsav will promote annual community-led maintenance and review of infrastructure. Coverage: JJM 2.0 aims to provide tap water connections to all 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028, with Gram Panchayats (GPs) achieving full coverage certified as ‘Har Ghar Jal’ villages. Overview of Jal Jeevan Mission: Launch: JJM was launched on 15 August 2019 by PM Narendra Modi to provide Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to all rural households in India. Implementation: The mission is implemented by the MoJS in partnership with State Governments and Union Territories (UTs). Target: The scheme targets 55 litres per capita per day (LPCD) of safe drinking water to every rural household. Components: Under JJM, key components include convergence of funds, development of in-village piped water supply for rural tap connections, augmentation of sustainable drinking water sources, bulk water transfer and treatment systems, and technological solutions for contaminant removal.

# Page 7^page=7
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 7 Progress: Since the launch, rural households with tap water connections increased from 3.23 crore (17%) to 15.80 crore (about 81.6%) out of 19.36 crore households by March 2026, with over 12.56 crore new connections added. Impact of JJM: Women: According to State Bank of India (SBI) Research, the JJM has freed around 9 crore women from the daily burden of fetching water. Health: A study by the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that access to safe drinking water under JJM could prevent around 4 lakh diarrhoeal deaths and save 14 million Disability Adjusted Life Years (DALYs). Mortality: Nobel Laureate (in Economics) Michael Kremer estimated that improved access to safe drinking water could reduce under-five child mortality by about 30%, saving nearly 1.36 lakh lives annually. Employment: Studies by the International Labour Organization (ILO) and Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bangalore (Karnataka) estimate that JJM has generated about 59.9 lakh direct and 2.2 crore indirect person-years of employment. About Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS): Union Minister– Chandrakant Raghunath (C R) Patil (Constituency-Navsari, Gujarat) Ministers of State (MoS)– Veeranna Somanna ( Constituency- Tumakuru, Karnataka ); Raj Bhushan Choudhary (Constituency- Muzaffarpur, Bihar) Sujalam: A national digital framework Sujalam Bharat will map the entire drinking water system from source to tap, assigning each village a Sujal Gaon / Service Area Identification (ID) for monitoring and transparency. Governance: The Jal Arpan mechanism will ensure transparent handover of water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats (GPs) and Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), while Jal Utsav will promote annual community-led maintenance and review of infrastructure. Cabinet Approves Amendments to FDI Rules for Investments from LBCs In March 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved amendments to India’s Foreign Direct Investments (FDI) framework governing investments from countries that share a Land Border Countries (LBCs). • The decision aims to streamline the approval process while ensuring national security and economic safeguards. • The rules apply to China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, and Afghanistan. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Union Cabinet approved FDI framework for investments from LBCs ✓ Purpose: Boost Investment inflows ✓ Countries Covered: China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Afghanistan ✓ BO Limit: Non-controlling beneficial ownership up to 10% allowed under the Automatic Route ✓ Approval Timeline: 60-day decision period for proposals. ✓ Key Sectors: Capital goods, electronic capital goods, electronic components, polysilicon, ingot- wafer manufacturing. ✓ Sector Revision: Can be revised by the Committee of Secretaries (CoS). Background: FDI Policy Amendment: To prevent opportunistic takeovers of Indian companies during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government of India (GoI) amended the FDI policy on 17 April 2020. Previous Provision: Under this provision, entities from LBCs, or investments where the beneficial owner is located in or is a citizen of such countries, can invest in India only through the Government approval

# Page 8^page=8
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 8 route. Impact of Restrictions: The application of such restrictions to non-strategic, non-controlling investments by LBC investors was considered to adversely affect investment inflows. Purpose: Now, these policy reforms aim to simplify regulatory procedures, promote technology collaborations, and boost investment inflows, especially in startups, deep-tech ventures, and manufacturing sectors. Investment Reforms: This revision introduces greater clarity in ownership assessment and establishes faster approval timelines for investments in selected strategic manufacturing sectors. Key Changes in FDI Rules: Beneficial Ownership(BO) Framework: BO in FDI refers to the natural person(s) who ultimately own, control, or receive the benefits from an investment, rather than just the registered legal entity. • Definition: The revised policy introduces a clear definition of BO aligned with standards under the Prevention of Money Laundering Rules (PMLR), 2005. The BO test will be applied at the investor entity level. • Automatic Route for Limited Investment: Investments where the beneficial owner from LBCs holds a non-controlling stake of up to 10% will now be permitted through the automatic route, subject to sectoral caps and regulatory conditions. • Disclosure Requirement: The investee company must disclose investment details to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I). Expedited Approval Mechanism: The amended policy introduces a 60-day decision timeline for investment proposals from LBCs in specific sectors. This approval timeline will help companies enter into joint ventures to access technologies, and integrate with global supply chains. • Sectors: These sectors are considered strategically important for India’s industrial and technology ecosystem. These specific manufacturing sectors include: Capital goods, Electronic capital goods, Electronic components, Polysilicon, and Ingot-wafer manufacturing. • Revision: The Committee of Secretaries (CoS), the high level inter-ministerial body within the Government of India (GoI) may also revise the list of specified sectors. • Domestic Control: In these cases, the majority shareholding and control of the Investee entity will be with resident Indian citizen(s) and/or Resident Indian (RI) entity(ies) owned and controlled by RI citizen(s), at all times. FDI Investment Routes in India: Automatic Route: Under this route, investors are allowed to invest in Indian companies without needing to seek prior approval from the government or any regulatory authority. Government Route: This route requires prior approval from the concerned ministry or department before an investment can be made. • Investments under this route are submitted through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP), which forwards the proposals to the relevant ministries for review and decision-making. About Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) was established in the year 1995 and was reconstituted in the year 2000 with the merger of the Department of Industrial Development.

# Page 9^page=9
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 9 • The department was earlier called Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion (DIPP) and was renamed as DPIIT in January, 2019. Secretary – Amardeep Singh Bhatia Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 1995 Cabinet Approvals on March 10, 2026: Major Infrastructure and Transport Projects Across India In March 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved several major infrastructure projects, including granting international airport status to Madurai Airport (Tamil Nadu, TN); Rs. 4,474 crore railway multitracking projects in West Bengal (WB) and Jharkhand, a Rs. 3,631 crore road project in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (UP), and a Rs. 3,839 crore highway widening project in Madhya Pradesh (MP). • The projects, approved under the Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan (PMGS- NMP), are intended to advance regional connectivity, streamline logistics, and foster economic development across India. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Union Cabinet approved major infrastructure and transport projects under PMGS-NMP ✓ Chair: PM Narendra Modi ✓ Key Approvals: ✓ Madurai Airport (TN): Declared International Airport (4th in TN) ✓ Railway Multitracking Projects: Rs 4,474 crore, ~192 km in WB & Jharkhand ✓ Greenfield Road to Jewar Airport: Rs 3,630.77 crore, 31.42 km corridor in UP & Haryana, implemented under Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). ✓ NH-752D Highway Project: Rs 3,839.42 crore, 80.45 km four-laning in MP, linking Ujjain to Delhi– Mumbai Expressway. Declaration of Madurai Airport (TN) as an International Airport: Approval: The Union Cabinet approved the declaration of Madurai Airport in TN as an International Airport. Position: With this upgrade, Madurai Airport becomes the fourth airport in TN to receive official international status, joining Chennai International Airport, Coimbatore International Airport, and Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) International Airport. Gateway: Located in Madurai, popularly known as the Temple City, Madurai Airport serves as a key gateway to Southern TN, supporting tourism, pilgrimage and regional connectivity. Impact: The international status is expected to enhance international connectivity, tourism, trade and economic development in the southern region of TN. Approval of Railway Multitracking Projects: Approval: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved two Indian Railways (IR) multitracking projects worth Rs 4,474 crore. Coverage: The projects span five districts across West Bengal (WB) and Jharkhand, expanding the IRs network by about 192 kilometres (km). Routes: The projects include construction of the fourth railway line between Sainthia–Pakur (WB and Jharkhand) and Santragachi–Kharagpur (WB). Connectivity: Improved rail infrastructure will benefit around 5,652 villages with an estimated population of about 1.47 crore people and enhance access to key tourist destinations. Freight: The capacity augmentation will enable additional freight movement of about 31 Million Tonnes

# Page 10^page=10
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 10 Per Annum (MTPA) for commodities such as coal, cement, iron and steel, foodgrains and containers. Environment: The projects are expected to save about 0.6 crore litres of oil and reduce 28 crore kilograms (kg) of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, equivalent to planting around 1 crore trees. Approval of Greenfield Connectivity to Jewar International Airport: Approval: The CCEA approved the revised capital cost of Rs 3,630.77 crore for constructing Greenfield road connectivity to Noida International Airport , commonly known as Jewar International Airport, UP. Corridor: The project involves a 31.42 kilometre (km) corridor linking the Delhi–Faridabad–Ballabhgarh– Sohna spur of the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway (DME) across UP and Haryana . Mode: The project will be implemented under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) for infrastructure development. Connectivity: The corridor will provide high-speed access from South Delhi, Faridabad (Haryana) and Gurugram (Haryana) to Jewar International Airport, boosting regional connectivity in the National Capital Region (NCR) Delhi. Integration: The route intersects with the Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE), Yamuna Expressway (YE) and Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) enabling multimodal transport connectivity. Elevated: About 11 km of the corridor will be constructed as an elevated highway, forming a critical segment between Delhi–Noida Direct (DND)–Ballabhgarh Bypass and Jewar International Airport. Approval of NH-752D Four-Laning Project in Madhya Pradesh: Approval: CCEA approved a Rs 3,839.42 crore project for four-laning the Badnawar–Petlawad–Thandla– Timarwani section of National Highway-752D (NH-752D) in MP. Corridor: The project covers 80.45 km and will connect Ujjain with the Timarwani interchange on the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway (DME). Connectivity: The route forms the shortest corridor linking Gujarat and Maharashtra with Ujjain, strengthening inter-state connectivity and regional logistics. Efficiency: Upgradation from an intermediate lane to a four-lane highway will increase travel speeds and reduce travel time by about one hour. Regions: The corridor passes through the Dhar and Jhabua districts of MP, supporting development in tribal regions and areas under the National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP). Infrastructure: The highway will include 6 Major Bridges (MB), 34 Minor Bridges (mB), 1 Road Under Bridge (RUB), 9 Vehicular Underpasses (VUPs), 29 Light Vehicle Underpasses (LVUPs) and 4 Service Vehicle Underpasses (SVUPs). About Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan (PMGS-NMP): Launch: PMGS-NMP was launched on 13 October 2021 as a Rs 100 lakh crore initiative to transform India’s infrastructure development through integrated planning. Implementation: The programme is implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) in coordination with 16+ ministries and state governments to improve multimodal connectivity across Railways, Roads, Ports, Waterways, Airports, Mass Transport and Logistics Infrastructure. Platform: The plan operates on a Geographic Information System (GIS)-based digital platform developed by the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geoinformatics (BISAG-N). Technology: The platform integrates Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) satellite imagery and Survey of India (SoI) base maps and is hosted on the MeghRaj Government Cloud (MeghRaj) for coordinated infrastructure planning. About Madhya Pradesh(MP): Chief Minister (CM) – Mohan Yadav Governor – Mangubhai Chhanganbhai Patel

# Page 11^page=11
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 11 Capital – Bhopal Airport – Raja Bhoj International Airport, Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport Cabinet Approves Rs 33,660 crore ‘BHAVYA scheme’ to Develop 100 Plug-and-Play Industrial Parks On March 18, 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved Rs 33,660 crore Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA) scheme for developing 100 plug-and-play industrial parks across the country. • This newly approved scheme aims to develop world-class industrial infrastructure, unlocking manufacturing potential and driving India’s growth story. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval of new scheme ‘BHAVYA’ ✓ Approved by: Union Cabinet (chaired by PM Narendra Modi) ✓ Total Budget Allocated: Rs 33,660 crore ✓ Key Purpose: To develop nationwide 100 plug-and-play industrial parks ✓ Maximum Financial Support: Rs 1 crore per acre ✓ Infrastructure Eligible for Funds: Core infrastructure (internal roads, underground utilities, among others); Value-added infrastructure (ready-built factory sheds, testing labs, warehousing, among others) and Social infrastructure (worker housing and support amenities) ✓ Financial Support for External Infrastructure: 25% of Project Cost About BHAVYA Scheme: Implementation: BHAVYA scheme, structured on the success of Industrial Smart Cities developed under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) framework, will be implemented in partnership with states and private sector players. Project Selection Process: Under the new scheme, projects will be selected through a challenge mode to ensure only high-quality, reform-oriented and investment-readiness proposals. • Further, industrial parks ranging from 100 to 1000 acres will be undertaken for development. For Northeast and hilly areas, the minimum size for industrial parks can be 25 acres. Financial Assistance: The Government of India (GoI) will provide up to Rs1 crore per acre for: • Core infrastructure (internal roads, underground utilities, drainage, common treatment facilities, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and administrative systems) • Value-added infrastructure (ready-built factory sheds, built-to-suit units, testing labs, warehousing) • Social infrastructure (worker housing and support amenities) Allocation for External Infrastructure: The GoI has decided to allocate a maximum 25% of the project cost for external infrastructure, ensuring seamless connectivity and integration with existing networks. Expected Beneficiaries: The scheme is expected benefit: • Primary beneficiaries which include manufacturing units, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, and global investors seeking ready-to-use industrial infrastructure. • Secondary beneficiaries which include: workers, logistics providers, service sector enterprises, and local communities. Job Generation: BHAVYA scheme is expected to generate nearly 15 lakh direct jobs and support wider industrial expansion across manufacturing, logistics, and services sectors. Implementing Agency: National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC), under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I).

# Page 12^page=12
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 12 • At present, NICDC is implementing 20 projects across 13 states. About PM GatiShakti: Whole-of-Government Approach: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, is a “Whole-of- Government ” approach aimed to facilitate integrated planning of multimodal infrastructure through collaboration among the concerned ministries. Cost and Duration: The GoI had approved Rs 100 lakh crore for infrastructure development over the next five years. Key Drivers: It promotes integrated development across seven economic drivers—railways, roads, ports, waterways, airports, mass transport, and logistics—supported by energy, Information Technology (IT), water, and social infrastructure. Implementing Agency: The PMGS-NMP is currently being implemented by the MoC&I through the Logistics Division of the DPIIT. Digital Master Plan: It has been developed as a Digital Master Planning tool by Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geoinformatics (BISAG-N), Gandhinagar (Gujarat). About National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC): Chief Executive Officer (CEO) & Managing Director (MD) – Rajat Kumar Saini Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Incorporated – 2008 Cabinet Approves Rs.2584.60 crore ‘SHP Development Scheme’ To Boost Clean Energy Initiatives In March 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the ‘Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme’ for a period of 5 years (i.e. from Financial Year 2026- 27(FY27) to FY31), with total outlay of Rs.2584.60 crore. • This newly approved scheme is designed to install SHP projects of an approximate capacity of 1500 MegaWatt (MW) across the country. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval of SHP Development Scheme ✓ Approved by: Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi ✓ Outlay: Rs.2584.60 crore ✓ Duration: 5 years (FY27 to FY31) ✓ Target: To install SHP projects (approx. 1,500 MW) ✓ Implementing Agency: MNRE ✓ Project Size: 1–25 MW ✓ Central Financial Assistance: o For NE States: Rs 3.6 crore per MW or 30% of the project cost, (whichever is lower); maximum Rs.30 crore per project o For other states: Rs.2.4 crore per MW or 20% of project cost (whichever is lower), capped at Rs.20 crore per project. About Small Hydro Power Development Scheme: Implementing Agency: The scheme will be implemented by the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE). Maximum Energy Capacity: The new scheme will support small hydro projects ranging from 1 to 25 MW capacity to come up in different states. • The scheme specially focuses on hilly and North Eastern (NE) states with high potential for such projects.

# Page 13^page=13
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 13 Financial Support: Under SHP Development scheme, central financial assistance of Rs 3.6 crore per MW or 30% of the project cost, whichever is lower with an upper limit of Rs.30 crore per project will be provided to the NE states and in districts with international borders. • For other states, the government will provide financial support of Rs.2.4 crore per MW or 20% of project cost (whichever is lower), capped at Rs.20 crore per project. • Out of the total Rs 2,584.60 crore, Rs 2,532.60 crore is specifically for Central Financial Assistance (CFA). Alignment: The investment required for the scheme will use 100% of the plant and machinery from indigenous sources, aligning with Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. Technology: The initiative emphasises the use of eco-friendly ‘run-of-the-river’ technology that generates power directly from the natural flow of rivers without large dams. • It will help in mitigating displacement, deforestation and ecological disruption. Incentive Structure: Under the new scheme, the Government of India (GoI) has allocated Rs 30 crore to support State and Central Government agencies in preparing Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for around 200 projects, aimed at creating a pipeline of small hydro projects in the future. Economic Significance: The newly approved scheme is expected to attract investments worth Rs 15,000 crore, with a focus on tapping hydro potential in hilly, NE and border areas of the country, where grid connectivity remains limited. Employment: The scheme will support 51 lakh person days of jobs during the project construction period. • In addition, it will also generate jobs in maintenance and operation in largely rural and remote locations. About Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE): Union Minister- Pralhad Joshi (Constituency- Dharwad, Karnataka) Minister of State (MoS)- Shripad Yesso Naik (Rajya Sabha- North Goa, Goa) CCEA Approves Rs 1,718 Crore MSP Support for Cotton & Rs 6,969 Crore NH-927 Project in UP In March 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) chaired by Prime Minister(PM) Narendra Modi approved Minimum Support Price (MSP) funding of Rs 1,718.56 crore for cotton farmers and sanctioned a Rs. 6,969.04 crore National Highway (NH)-927 project in Uttar Pradesh (UP). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approved MSP support for cotton and NH-927 Project in UP ✓ Who? Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) ✓ MSP support: Approved Rs 1,718.56 crore MSP funding ✓ Cotton Production: 325.22 lakh bales (2023–24) ✓ NH project: Construction of 4-Lane Access-Controlled NH-927 project o Cost? Rs 6,969.04 crore Rs. 6,969.04 crore o Location: Barabanki to Bahraich (UP) o Implementing Agency: NHAI About MSP Support for Cotton: Approval: CCEA approved funding of Rs 1,718.56 crore to the Cotton Corporation of India Limited (CCI) for the 2023–24 cotton season. Objective: The funding provides price support to farmers when market prices fall below MSP, ensuring income security, preventing distress sales, and stabilising cotton prices. Livelihood: Cotton supports around 60 lakh farmers and 400–500 lakh people in allied sectors. Production: In 2023–24, India produced 325.22 lakh bales of cotton over 114.47 lakh hectares (ha), contributing nearly 25% of global cotton output. Pricing: MSP is fixed by Government of India (GoI) based on recommendations of Commission for

# Page 14^page=14
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 14 Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA&FW). About NH-927 Project Approval: Project: CCEA approved a 4-lane access-controlled National Highway 927 (NH-927) from Barabanki to Bahraich (101.515 kilometer, km) in UP. Cost: Total project cost is Rs. 6,969.04 crore under Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM), including Rs. 3,485.49 crore civil cost and Rs. 1,574.85 crore land acquisition cost. Connectivity: Enhances connectivity across 3 economic, 2 social, and 12 logistics nodes, reducing travel time to ~1 hour while improving road safety, fuel efficiency, and vehicle operating costs. Border: Strengthens India–Nepal connectivity via Rupaidiha Land Port (RLP) and boosts cross-border trade, tourism, and commerce. Development: Generates 36.54 lakh (direct) and 43.04 lakh (indirect) person-days of employment while improving connectivity to Bahraich and Shravasti districts and supporting Prime Minister GatiShakti – National Master Plan (PMGS – NMP) (launched in 2021). About Cotton Corporation of India (CCI): Role: CCI is the central nodal agency for Minimum Support Price (MSP) operations, procuring Fair Average Quality (FAQ) cotton without quantity limits when prices fall below MSP. Status: CCI is a Mini Ratna company under the Ministry of Textiles (MoT). Network: Operates over 508 procurement centres across 152 districts in 11 states and implements Bale Identification and Traceability System (BITS) and Cott-Ally app. Chairman and Managing Director (CMD)- Lalit Kumar Gupta Headquarters – Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra Established – 1970 Union Cabinet Approves Revamped UDAN Scheme to Strengthen Air Connectivity In March 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the launch and implementation of the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) – Modified Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik (UDAN), aimed at strengthening regional air connectivity and expanding aviation infrastructure across the country. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Union Cabinet approves revamped UDAN ✓ Timeline: 10-year period – FY27 to FY36 ✓ Financial Outlay: Rs 28,840 Cr ✓ New Destinations: 120 ✓ Key Components: o Aerodromes: 100 airports, Rs 12,159 Cr, 8 years o O&M Aerodromes: 3 years, Rs 3.06 Cr/airport, Rs 0.90 Cr/ helicopter, Rs 2,577 Cr o Modern Helipads: 200, Rs 3661 Crs – 8 years o VGF: Rs 10,043 Cr, 10 years o Aircraft Acquisition: 400 Cr, 2 HAL Dhruv helicopters, 2 HAL dornier aircraft Key Highlights Objective: The revamped programme aims to deepen regional air connectivity, especially in underserved and unserved areas. • It is also expected to drive economic growth, trade and tourism in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities Timeline: The scheme will be implemented over a 10-year period from Financial Year 2026-27 (FY27) to FY36. Financial Outlay: The total financial outlay of the scheme is Rs 28,840 crore (Cr).

# Page 15^page=15

Legislative: Under Articles 174–176 and Article 200, the Governor summons, prorogues, or dissolves the Legislative Assembly, addresses the Legislature, and can assent to, withhold, or reserve Bills for the President. Ordinance: Article 213 authorizes the Governor to promulgate ordinances when the Legislature is not in session.
